prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite sheet for a cute hand-painted 2D chibi desktop character, arcade UFO claw-machine mechanism. Create exactly FOUR isolated mechanical component sprites, separated into a spacious 2 by 2 grid on a genuinely transparent canvas, with no text or labels. TOP LEFT: a short vertical telescopic mechanical arm with a silver piston, orange protective upper casing, and a small round silver claw hub at its bottom; approximately 2.5 times taller than wide. TOP RIGHT: ONE straight thin rigid silver claw linkage, vertical, with a round pivot hole / warm dark bolt at each end; approximately 8 times taller than wide. BOTTOM LEFT: ONE left-side curved silver claw finger, opening toward the RIGHT: circular pivot at its upper left, a long slim crescent metal shaft curving gently to the lower right, ending in a rounded inward hook with a small dark charcoal rubber pad. Approximately 3 times taller than wide. BOTTOM RIGHT: ONE narrow rear third claw finger with a top circular pivot, straight slightly curved slim silver shaft, and a tiny rounded inward hook at its lower end. Approximately 7 times taller than wide. Render in warm anime storybook hand-drawn style: variable-width warm dark-brown ink outlines, silver and pale blue-gray metal, darker blue-gray edge shadows, small warm orange accents, restrained cream highlights, brush shading. Clear mechanical contours and tidy antialiased edges, all components complete and uncropped, separate pieces must NOT touch each other. These are arcade toy-grabbing components, friendly rounded metal rather than sharp blades; no saw teeth, no sharp points, no character, no stuffed toy, no assembled machine, no drop shadows outside the components, no background, no scenery, no checkerboard painted into the pixels. Preserve real transparent alpha around each sprite.
purpose: Split painted rigid mechanical components, preserve generated alpha; no repainting of the character.
